 GameNative's new update brings reliable PC gaming to Pixels and Samsung Exynos
 Android Police Follow Mark Jansen Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:47 PM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:47 PM UTC Mark Jansen/Android Police GameNative , the app that lets users play PC games on their Android smartphones, has released a major new update .
 In GameNative 1.4.1, players not using a Snapdragon chip will finally have the chance to properly play their games, thanks to an update that makes the software much more reliable on a number of phone's GPUs.
 Play PC games on your Pixel or Exynos Galaxy phone
 Update brings much wider support for non-Snapdragon chips
 Mark Jansen/Android Police
 GameNative has been around for a while now, and while it's one of the best ways to run PC games locally on your smartphone , it does have some major issues preventing even the most enthusiastic gamers from playing. Namely, it didn't always play nice with phones that weren't running Qualcomm Snapdragon hardware.
 Advertisement Advertisement While it was certainly possible to run GameNative on a Pixel , or a Samsung Galaxy phone with an Exynos processor, it wasn't the best experience. Crashes were common, and sometimes, supported games would simply refuse to launch.
 Those issues should hopefully be a thing of the past with GameNative 1.4.1. Released on GitHub as a preview build , this build finally fixes many of the problems other processors and GPUs have been having with GameNative.
 GameNative
 The update specifically targets devices with Mali, PowerVR, and Xclipse GPUs, which includes most Pixels and Samsung Exynos phones. As you can see from the table above, the fixes target many devices, which means GameNative is now a more tempting proposition for many.
 The Samsung Galaxy S24 and S26 ranges are two notable inclusions here, as well as mentions of Pixels from the Pixel 6 to last year's Pixel 10 . The Pixel 11 is oddly missing for some reason, and it's possible that phone range may continue to have problems running GameNative properly.
 Advertisement Advertisement It's important to note that this update is not likely to make any games that weren't previously compatible suddenly playable. Instead, it's meant to make the games that should work, actually work.
 Mark Jansen/Android Police
 It can't really be understated how important this update will be for wide adoption of GameNative for gamers. The Google Pixel may not be the most popular phone around, but it's certainly amongst the most popular, and even if its hardware has traditionally not been great for gaming, it's still a very capable phone range that can run a number of older PC titles.
 But far more important is the inclusion of Exynos Samsung devices. Exynos is far more common in Samsung devices outside the US, with many of Samsung's flagships, including the Galaxy S range, using Samsung's Exynos processors. By adding reliability to GameNative for those devices, it's likely to buy itself a much larger audience.
 You can download GameNative from GitHub as an APK that you'll then need to install independently of the Google Play Store .
